en.authority: Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs / e-Sbírka; English synthesis from the officially published treaty text
en.text: Article 10 — Dividends. Dividends paid by a company resident in one Contracting State to a resident of the other State may also be taxed in the State of the paying company. If the beneficial owner is a company that directly holds at least 10 per cent of the capital of the paying company, the source-State tax shall not exceed 5 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends. In other cases where the recipient is the beneficial owner, the source-State tax shall not exceed 10 per cent.

en.authority: Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs / e-Sbírka; English synthesis from the officially published treaty text
en.text: Article 11 — Interest. Interest arising in one Contracting State and beneficially owned by a resident of the other Contracting State is taxable only in that other State. The treaty therefore assigns no source-State withholding tax to qualifying interest, subject to the Article's permanent-establishment and special-relationship provisions.

en.authority: Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs / e-Sbírka; English synthesis from the officially published treaty text
en.text: Article 12 — Royalties. Royalties arising in one Contracting State and paid to a resident of the other State may also be taxed in the source State if the recipient is the beneficial owner. The source-State tax shall not exceed 5 per cent of the gross amount for copyright royalties concerning literary, artistic or scientific works, including cinematograph films. It shall not exceed 10 per cent for royalties concerning patents, trademarks, designs or models, plans, secret formulae or processes, customised computer software, industrial, commercial or scientific equipment, or industrial, commercial or scientific experience.
